items.title: How Cornell Punished Each of the 7 Men Accused of Sexual Assault
items.author: Sharon Otterman, Hurubie Meko and Debra Kamin
items.content: <article>Summaries obtained by The New York Times offer a detailed look at the discipline meted out to the men accused of sexually assaulting a fellow student at Cornell University.</article>

items.title: Here’s Senator Cotton’s Cell Number, Trump Says, in Dispute Over Daylight Saving Bill
items.author: Mack Liederman and Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>The president urged people to call Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas and accused him of blocking a bill to cement daylight saving time.</article>

items.title: Cornell President Calls Rape Inquiry ‘Defining Moment’ for Campus
items.author: Claire Fahy
items.content: <article>Michael I. Kotlikoff said in a video the university would be more transparent, hold Greek groups accountable and improve sexual assault prevention.</article>

items.title: ‘Digger,’ Warner Bros.’ Last Release Before Merger, Is a Major Flop
items.author: Nicole Sperling
items.content: <article>The film, starring Tom Cruise, grossed an estimated $8 million in its opening weekend. That could put the movie on track to lose at least $125 million.</article>

items.title: Tennessee Commissioner Resigns After Failed Execution of Christa Pike
items.author: Emily Cochrane
items.content: <article>Frank Strada, who oversaw the process that left Christa Pike unconscious and hospitalized, quit as an independent review began.</article>

items.title: American High School Students Are Selling Guns Bound for Cartels
items.author: Paulina Villegas and Adriana Zehbrauskas
items.content: <article>Drawn by money and status, teenagers in Arizona are buying, stealing and selling weapons destined for criminal groups in Mexico.</article>

items.title: What We Learned About American Teenagers Supplying Guns to Cartels
items.author: Paulina Villegas
items.content: <article>Our reporting revealed how Mexican criminal groups are relying on teenagers and young adults in border states like Arizona to help supply their weapons.</article>

items.title: Chris Rock Has Been Thinking About Forgiveness
items.author: David Marchese
items.content: <article>The comedian and filmmaker on what real friendship looks like, what keeps him up at night and his new movie, “Misty Green.”</article>

items.title: Trump’s War Empowers Extremists in Iran
items.author: Nicholas Kristof
items.content: <article>Threats to withdraw from the Nuclear Nonproliferation Treaty are growing in Tehran.</article>

items.title: Cornell Case Revives Anger About Handling of Campus Sexual Assault Cases
items.author: Stephanie Saul and Emma Goldberg
items.content: <article>A lawsuit alleging rape at Cornell has led to an outpouring of women sharing stories about sexual violence on college campuses.</article>

items.title: ‘How Does That Happen?’: America’s Execution System Is Long Flawed
items.author: Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
items.content: <article>The failed execution of Christa Pike, which left her clinging to life in Tennessee, was the latest grisly error to take place in an American execution chamber.</article>

items.title: Senate Races in Republican States Tilt Toward Democrats, Polls Find
items.author: Patricia Mazzei, Ruth Igielnik and Sophia June
items.content: <article>Democrats are performing strongly in five reliably Republican states where they are trying to flip Senate seats to win control of the chamber, new New York Times/Siena polls found.</article>

items.title: The Middle School Kids Trying to Make Sense of Stalin’s Tyranny
items.author: Ora DeKornfeld and Bianca Giaever
items.content: <article>Middle school introduces us to complicated history. These kids wrote a play about Joseph Stalin.</article>
